name: a(n) is the smallest integer k such that the number of sums a(i) + a(j) <= k for i <= j < n is less than k - n + 1.
comment: Erdős asks if the number of solutions a(i) + a(j) <= k is equal to k + O(k^(1/4+o(1))) (see Erdős Problems link).
link: William Alexander Carney, Table of n, a(n) for n = 1..1200
example: a(3) = 5 because k = 5 is the least integer such that the number of sums for the first two terms {1, 3} that are less than 5 is 2: 1 + 1 = 2 and 3 + 1 = 4 and 2 is less than 5 - 3 + 1.
author: _Giorgos Kalogeropoulos_, Nov 13 2025
